issues.description: Template StockIngredient defines a getter named 'retrieveQuantity()' while other classes (Stock) and the exercise instructions expect a standard getter 'getQuantity()'. This causes a structural mismatch: Stock.java calls getQuantity() but no such method exists in the template, so the template code will not compile and students will be confused about which getter name to implement. The solution repository uses getQuantity(), matching the problem statement requirement to add getters for all private fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method retrieveQuantity() in the template StockIngredient to getQuantity(), or add a getQuantity() delegating to retrieveQuantity(). This ensures Stock.java's calls to getQuantity() compile and matches the solution and the problem's instruction to provide standard getters for all private fields.

issues.description: The template repository defines the quantity accessor in StockIngredient as retrieveQuantity(), whereas the problem statement asks for getters for private fields (implying conventional getX naming) and the solution implements getQuantity(). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual getter (quantity of a StockIngredient) creates confusion for students mapping the problem requirements to the template and solution and may cause compilation/usage mismatches in Stock and SealSaloon code that expect getQuantity().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template accessor retrieveQuantity() to the conventional getter name getQuantity() (and update all call sites) so the template, problem statement expectations, and solution use the same identifier for the quantity getter. Ensure Stock and other classes call getQuantity().
